title: Integrator Cookbook: lite quickstart + telemetry bench notes
content:
Purpose and audience:
This is a lightweight, opinionated cookbook for integrator teams (internal platform teams + early customers) who need a quick, repeatable path to get an SDK-driven feature from hello-world to a monitored, cost-aware pilot. Focus is practical: the smallest set of steps that unblock a production-ish trial, plus a compact telemetry bench to validate latency/cost assumptions.

Why a separate integrator flow?
- Integrators expect sample code + known observability hooks; they juggle several product integrations simultaneously.
- Full-blown onboarding docs are heavy; this doc prioritizes the 2–4 hour path and stops at an operational pitstop: basic SLO, cost baseline, and a rollback trigger.

High-level flow (pitstops):
1) Local smoke: authenticate + sample request + human-verify output (15–30m)
2) Instrumented run: send realistic traffic with telemetry, capture P95 and token-cost baseline (1–2h)
3) Safety/UX checks: prompt sanitization + fallback behavior test (30–60m)
4) Canary / limited rollout to a sandbox customer segment (4–24h)
5) Post-mortem and lock-in checklist: quality regression checks + cost optimization plan (30–90m)

Quickstart (minimal commands and expectations)
- Goals: have one integration calling Redwood API + collect the following metrics: request-id, model, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_usd_estimate.
- Pre-reqs: API key, small sample prompt set, simple harness (curl or node/python script).

Example curl smoke (do this first):
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-1-small","input":"Summarize: The quick brown fox..."}'

What to verify after smoke: human-readable response; correlation id present in headers; documented error codes seen (429, 500) behave as expected.

Minimal instrumented harness (conceptual)
- One script that: iterates over sample prompts, calls the API, records: request_id, latency_ms, rc (HTTP code), tokens_in, tokens_out, model.
- Run 100 sequential requests to mimic interactive traffic, then 100 parallel requests (concurrency = 8) to observe queue/backpressure behavior.
- Export results to CSV for quick pivots into spreadsheet if needed.

Compact telemetry bench (recommended events and fields)
Event names and required fields (keeps dashboards small):
- rwd.request (request_id, model, user_tier, latency_ms, rc, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_estimate_usd)
- rwd.model.switch (request_id, from_model, to_model, reason)
- rwd.cache.hit (request_id, prefix_key, cached_tokens_saved)
- rwd.error (request_id, error_type, message, retried)

Bench thresholds to collect initially (these are starting heuristics):
- P50 latency target: < 60ms for small models, < 220ms for medium opts in hosted mode
- P95 latency: use as main signal for alerting — trigger if deviates +40% vs baseline
- Retry rate: target < 1% for clean traffic
- Cost delta: initial cost_estimate_usd per 1k requests establishes budget; flag if > 30% above initial baseline within 48h

Suggested lightweight dashboard tiles
- Latency distribution (P50 / P95 / P99) per model and per route
- Token consumption rate (tokens_in/out per minute) with rolling 1h window
- Errors by type (4xx/5xx/timeout) + recent examples for quick triage
- Cost burn rate (USD per hour and rolling 24h)

Failure modes to test (and quick mitigations)
- Spike in tail latency: verify autoscaling and warmup behaviors; mitigate by reducing concurrency or switching to a cheaper low-latency model variant.
- Prompt regression (nonsensical output): detect with sample prompts, rollback to previous model version, toggle quality guardrails (function-calling, temperature limits)
- Unexplained cost bump: re-run harness with logging of tokens_in/out per request and correlate with model switch events

Prompt hygiene checklist (short):
- Ensure we send a max_input_tokens cap from client side to avoid runaway costs
- Normalize user-supplied content (strip huge attachments, collapse whitespace)
- Add explicit system instruction header where appropriate so model variant switching preserves behavior

Telemetry sampling guidance
- For high-volume flows, sample 1% of requests but always sample failures + model-switch events.
- For pilot/integrator trials, sample 100% for first 24–48h.

Rollout decision matrix (quick):
- Keep canary running if: P95 <= baseline*1.25 AND error rate <= 1% AND cost drift <= 15%
- Roll back immediately if: P95 > baseline*1.5 OR error rate > 5% OR any safety violation flagged in evals

Open design questions / TODOs (for team sync)
- How do we surface model variant compatibility to integrators without exposing internal catalog complexity? (Decide: simple "low-latency" / "high-quality" labels?)
- Should SDK expose an opt-in telemetry wrapper that emits rwd.* events by default? (Security + PII considerations)
- What is the minimum set of prompts for automated quality regression checks in our infra? (action: Priya to propose a 20-prompt seed set)

Action items (short)
- Ari: wire up a reference harness repo (node + python) with the minimal instrumentation above by 2024-12-15.
- Maya: draft a short SDK README that explains the telemetry event contract and sample dashboard queries by 2024-12-05.
- Priya: propose seed regression prompt bank and initial sampling rules by 2024-12-12.

Appendix: sample CSV columns for quick import
request_id, timestamp_iso, model, route, user_tier, latency_ms, rc, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_estimate_usd, sample_prompt_id

Notes to self (informal)
- Keep this doc intentionally small. Integrators hate long-winded policy prose at first touch.
- We can expand individual pitstops into full templates later (playbook for canary, playbook for cost regression), but only if adoption shows friction here.

References (internal)
- see linked artifacts above for the Integrator index + the in-progress harness PR

End of draft.
